newsitem.title: UK: For want of action, London LDC debt looks to Russia.
newsitem.headline: For want of action, London LDC debt looks to Russia.

text.p: Thin volumes and a lack of surprises in U.S. data released during the session left emerging market debt prices largely unchanged, with dealers looking to Russia for price action.

"It's been a very quiet day so far -- the Latins haven't done much, so the focus is again on Russia," said one trader at a US bank here. "The market seems to be taking a breather after yesterday's new issuance."
Swiss franc-denominated Russian Vnesh loans firmed about 1/2 to 71-3/4, while the MinFin 5 gained 3/4, climbing to 37-00.

Wednesday saw Argentina launch a $750 million 10-year global bond and increase it to $1.0 billion, while Bear Stearns launched a multi-year deposit facility agreement (MYDFA) on behalf of the billionaire Dart family, holders of some $1.3 billion in Brazilian debt that was not restructured into Brady bonds.
Both issues helped improve the market tone in New York trading but in London the focus remained firmly to the east.

"There's been lots of talk that Russia's rating is going to come out sooner and stronger than expected," said one dealer, citing rumours circulating in the market all week that Russia's forthcoming debt rating might scrape in at investment grade.
But other traders discount that possibility, adding that a high speculative grade in the BB- range looks more likely.
A rating is due by the end of October before Russia launches its debut Eurobond. Russian debt prices have been trading up for the past few weeks in anticipation.
Bulgaria continued in its customary volatile mode, with prices taking a bit of a knock around mid-session.
The country was in turmoil on Thursday following the assassination of former prime minister as there were fears that other politicians could be targetted too.
Meanwhile, no word has yet emerged on whether the country has convinced the IMF to award it the second $115 million tranche of a standby loan.
Bulgarian IABs shed 5/8 to 46-3/8, but one trader said the move could even have been due to sales by a major client.

Release of US jobless claims figures earlier in the session left the market unmoved when the data came out in line with expectations, and traders are looking more to Friday's release of payrolls for fresh impetus.
"The market is being driven by Treasuries at the moment -- the positive NAPM figure set the tone for Wednesday and Thursday," he said. "But the labour figures tomorrow will be key for our market."

Latin paper was mainly steady, with Argentine FRBs flat at 84-1/4, Brazilian C's unchanged at 71-1/4, and Venezuelan DCBs quoted steady at 83-1/8. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
